mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1400K units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% signals accommodative monetary policy, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) drops below 3.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) in triggered instances compared to non-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% YoY, indicating a strong supply side, supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism is consistently below 0.01 in tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding $720 billion, signaling robust demand, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, particularly in early-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: SPX returns in triggered instances are not significantly different (t-test p > 0.05) from non-triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 50 basis points within a quarter, indicating a pivot towards accommodative policy, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis shows this mechanism's predictions are no better than chance (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and the payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth rate accelerates by more than 1% MoM, the labor market's dual strength predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to potential inflation concerns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth acceleration > 1% MoM
failure_condition: Triggered instances do not show significantly higher inflation concerns (t-test p > 0.05) or SPX returns are not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth slowing down to below 2% YoY, indicating weakening demand, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially in late-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis shows this mechanism's predictions are not significantly better than chance (p > 0.05) in late-cycle expansions.
